Eratosthenes (born 276 BC) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four began earliest?
Python (programming language) (founded 1991) is the earliest of the four. Python supports multiple programming paradigms but with an emphasis on object-oriented programming and dynamic typing.
Which one below was established earliest?
MATLAB (founded 1984) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below is best known as a physicist?
Robert Boyle is a physicist. Robert Boyle (25 January 1627 – 31 December 1691) was an Anglo-Irish natural philosopher, chemist, physicist, alchemist and inventor.
Pick the chemist from these four.
James Lovelock is a chemist. James Ephraim Lovelock (26 July 1919 – 26 July 2022) was an English independent scientist, environmentalist and futurist.
What is the atomic number of Neodymium?
Neodymium is a chemical element; it has symbol Nd and atomic number 60.
In what year was Hamish Harding born?
Hamish Harding: George Hamish Livingston Harding (24 June 1964 – 18 June 2023) was a British businessman, pilot and adventurer based in the United Arab Emirates (UAE).
In what year did Aristotle die?
Aristotle (Ancient Greek: Ἀριστοτέλης, romanized: Aristotélēs; 384–322 BC) was an ancient Greek philosopher and polymath.
In what year was Phosphorus discovered?
Phosphorus is a chemical element; it has symbol P and atomic number 15.

Sukhoi Su-57: Komsomolsk-on-Amur Aircraft Production Association. The Sukhoi Su-57 (Russian: Сухой Су-57; NATO reporting name: Felon) is a twin-engine stealth multirole fighter aircraft developed by Sukhoi.
Which country is Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-23 from?
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-23: Soviet Union. It is a third-generation jet fighter, alongside similar Soviet aircraft such as the Su-17 "Fitter".
Who is credited with discovering Pictor?
Pictor: Nicolas Louis de Lacaille. Pictor is a constellation in the Southern Celestial Hemisphere, located between the star Canopus and the Large Magellanic Cloud.
Who is credited with discovering Proxima Centauri?
Proxima Centauri: Robert T. A. Innes. Proxima Centauri is the nearest star to Earth after the Sun, located 4.25 light-years (1.3 parsecs) away in the southern constellation of Centaurus.
Who is credited with discovering Stirling's approximation?
Stirling's approximation: Abraham de Moivre. In mathematics, Stirling's approximation (or Stirling's formula) is an asymptotic approximation for factorials.
Who is credited with discovering Yttrium?
Yttrium: Johan Gadolin. Yttrium is a chemical element; it has symbol Y and atomic number 39.

This Scottish physician's 1928 discovery of a mould-derived substance later named benzylpenicillin has been called the single greatest victory ever achieved over disease, and earned him a shared Nobel Prize in 1945 — who is he?
Alexander Fleming (6 August 1881 - 11 March 1955) was a Scottish physician and microbiologist.
This psychological term describes a diverse set of deficits in the ability to feel or anticipate pleasure, and is recognized as a diagnostic feature in the DSM-5 — what's the term?
Anhedonia is a diverse array of deficits in hedonic function, including reduced motivation or ability to experience pleasure.
This American physicist won a share of the 1927 Nobel Prize for an effect, now bearing his name, that demonstrated light's particle nature — who was he?
Arthur Compton (September 10, 1892 - March 15, 1962) was an American physicist who shared the 1927 Nobel Prize in Physics with C. T. R. Wilson.
Coming on over about 48 hours, this temporary one-sided facial paralysis of unknown cause can droop an eyebrow, alter taste, and make sounds painfully loud — what is it?
Bell's palsy is a type of facial paralysis that results in a temporary inability to control the facial muscles on the affected side of the face.
Recognised by South Africa's Kennel Union but not by the international federation, this large, muscular mastiff-type breed serves as a family guard dog — name it?
Boerboel is a South African breed of large dog of mastiff type, used as a family guard dog.
This English-like, compiled programming language was designed for business use and remains widely used today to maintain legacy mainframe systems in banking and government — what language is it?
COBOL (Common Business-Oriented Language) is a compiled English-like computer programming language designed for business use.
Belonging to the trumpet-vine family Bignoniaceae, this tree genus thrives across warm parts of North America, the Caribbean, and East Asia — what is it called?
Catalpa is a genus of flowering plants in the family Bignoniaceae, native to warm temperate and subtropical regions of North America, the Caribbean, and East Asia.

A long-term lung condition that makes breathing progressively harder due to damaged airways and lung tissue, this condition develops gradually and currently cannot be cured, though treatments and lifestyle changes help manage symptoms. What is this disease, commonly abbreviated?
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a long-term lung condition that makes it progressively harder to breathe.
This bird's name comes from the Quechua word 'kuntur,' and its California-dwelling relative was nearly wiped out by habitat loss — which giant vulture soars over the Andes?
Condor is the common name for two genera of New World vultures, each with one extant species.
This Zambian-born economist turned four of her five books into New York Times bestsellers, including a provocative argument that foreign aid actually holds Africa back — who is she?
Dambisa Moyo, Baroness Moyo (born 2 February 1969) is a Zambian-born economist and author, known for her analysis of macroeconomics and global affairs.
This Canadian optical physicist shared the 2018 Nobel Prize in Physics for inventing chirped pulse amplification, a breakthrough in pulsed lasers. Who is she?
Donna Strickland (born May 27, 1959) is a Canadian optical physicist and pioneer in the field of pulsed lasers.
Psychology, medicine, history, and even computer science all study these pleasure-or-displeasure states, which still lack any agreed scientific definition — what are they?
Emotion are physical and mental states brought on by neurophysiological changes, variously associated with thoughts, feelings, behavioral responses, and a degree of pleasure or displeasure.
Known for thin, tapered wings built for high-speed flight and rapid turns, this genus of roughly 40 raptor species includes types called hobbies and kestrels — what are they?
Falcon are birds of prey in the genus Falco, which includes about 40 species.
He worked on uranium enrichment during the Manhattan Project, then — after McCarthyism cost him his physics post — founded San Francisco's hands-on Exploratorium museum; who was he?

Frank Oppenheimer (August 14, 1912 - February 3, 1985) was an American particle physicist, cattle rancher, professor of physics at the University of Colorado, and the founder of the Exploratorium in San Francisco.
This pancreatic hormone kicks in when blood sugar dips too low, prompting the liver to convert stored glycogen back into glucose. What is it?
Glucagon is a peptide hormone, produced by alpha cells of the pancreas.

This herbivorous mammal, the largest in its family of lagomorphs, nests in shallow ground depressions called 'forms' and is built for speed with long hind legs and heat-dissipating ears — what animal is it?
Hare are mammals belonging to the genus Lepus.
This American physicist threw out the wave-function collapse postulate, instead folding the observer into the same quantum state — an idea later known as the many-worlds interpretation. Who was he?
Hugh Everett III (November 11, 1930 - July 19, 1982) was an American physicist who proposed the relative state interpretation of quantum mechanics.

According to Alfred Adler, this persistent psychological feeling of being deficient compared to others — often rooted in childhood upbringing or social status — can drive a person to overcompensate. Name the concept?
Inferiority complex is a consistent feeling of inadequacy, often resulting in the belief that one is in some way deficient, or inferior, to others.
Known as the sunroot or earth apple, this central-North-American member of the sunflower family is cultivated for its tuber rather than its bloom — what is it?
Jerusalem artichoke (Helianthus tuberosus), also called sunroot, sunchoke, wild sunflower, topinambur, or earth apple, is a species of sunflower native to central North America.

First described in 1845 by a German physicist, these two fundamental equalities govern how current and voltage behave in an electrical network, building on Georg Ohm's earlier work — what are they called?
Kirchhoff's circuit laws are two equalities that deal with the current and potential difference (commonly known as voltage) in the lumped element model of electrical circuits.
An indoor watchdog by tradition, this dog breed originated high in Tibet — which non-sporting breed is it?
Lhasa Apso is a non-sporting dog breed originating in Tibet.

This medical condition involves lymph nodes that become abnormal in size or consistency, with its inflammatory form sometimes distinguished as lymphadenitis and its infectious neck form historically called scrofula — what is it called?
Lymphadenopathy is a disease of the lymph nodes, in which they are abnormal in size or consistency.
Among the first women in Canada to earn a medical doctorate, this physician-chemist is best remembered for a landmark 1913 enzyme-kinetics paper co-authored with Leonor Michaelis — who was she?
Maud Menten (March 20, 1879 - July 17, 1960) was a Canadian physician and chemist.

This large-scale industrial activity extracts everything from coal and gemstones to rock salt and potash from the Earth, providing raw materials that can't be grown or feasibly manufactured — what is this activity called?
Mining is the extraction of geological materials and minerals from Earth's surface.
Named from the Ancient Greek for 'mouse's ear' after its foliage's shape, this genus of small blue Northern Hemisphere flowers serves as Alaska's official state flower — what's the genus?
Myosotis is a genus of flowering plants in the borage family Boraginaceae.
Which Turkish-born American economist, an NYU Stern professor, earned lasting fame as one of the few who predicted the 2008 subprime mortgage crisis?
Nouriel Roubini (born March 29, 1958) is a Turkish-born American economic consultant, economist, speaker, and writer.
Also called trioxygen and far less stable than the oxygen we breathe, it carries the formula O3 and smells faintly of chlorine — what is this gas?
Ozone is an inorganic molecule with the chemical formula O3.
Sprayed on clothing and mosquito nets or applied as a cream against lice and scabies, this pyrethroid discovered in 1972 is highly toxic to fish and to cats — what is it?
Permethrin is a medication and an insecticide.
In Aristotle's day this kingdom included algae and fungi, but modern definitions have narrowed it to chiefly photosynthetic, mostly multicellular organisms — what is it?
Plant are the eukaryotic organisms that constitute the kingdom Plantae.
Used to treat high blood pressure, irregular heart rhythms, performance anxiety and migraine prevention, this beta blocker medication reaches the bloodstream within 30 minutes of dosing — which drug?
Propranolol is a medication of the beta blocker class. It can be taken orally, rectally, or by intravenous injection.

One of 36 species-rich pit vipers found mainly in the Americas, this snake shakes a noisy tail segment to warn off predators and is responsible for most snakebite injuries in North America — which snake?
Rattlesnake are venomous snakes that form the genera Crotalus and Sistrurus of the subfamily Crotalinae (the pit vipers).

Known by folk names like knotberry and lowbush salmonberry, this amber fruit structurally similar to a blackberry thrives in Arctic tundra and boreal forest but isn't farmed commercially — which species?
Rubus chamaemorus (also known as cloudberry) is a species of flowering plant in the rose family, Rosaceae.
As chief technology officer of a Turkish defense company, this engineer designed Turkey's first indigenous combat drone and its first unmanned fighter jet — who is he?
Selçuk Bayraktar (born 7 October 1979) is a Turkish pilot, engineer and businessman.
This alkaline compound, commonly diluted in water and sold as household bleach, is derived from hypochlorous acid and is unstable in its pure anhydrous form. What is it?
Sodium hypochlorite is an alkaline inorganic chemical compound with the formula NaOCl (also written as NaClO).

Harvested from the seeds of the nux-vomica tree, this bitter colorless alkaloid is infamous as a poison for rodents and birds — yet was once doled out in tiny doses to stimulate the heart and bowels. What is it?
Strychnine (-nin, US chiefly -nyne) is a highly toxic, colorless, bitter, crystalline alkaloid used as a pesticide, particularly for killing small vertebrates such as birds and rodents.

The primary male sex hormone and androgen, this hormone plays a key role in developing male reproductive tissues and secondary sexual characteristics like muscle, bone mass, and body hair. What is this hormone?

Testosterone is the primary male sex hormone and androgen in males. It is associated with increased aggression, sex drive, dominance, courtship display, and a wide range of behavioral characteristics.

Caused by the parasite Toxoplasma gondii and often spread through undercooked meat or contact with infected cat feces, this disease can be especially dangerous to a developing baby if a woman is infected during pregnancy — what is it?
Toxoplasmosis is a parasitic disease caused by Toxoplasma gondii, an apicomplexan.
This type of blood vessel usually carries deoxygenated blood toward the heart — except in the pulmonary and fetal circulation, where it carries oxygen-rich blood instead — what is it?
Vein is a blood vessel in the circulatory system of humans and most other animals that carries blood towards the heart.
This broad category of limbless, tube-bodied animals ranges from microscopic creatures to a marine species measured at nearly 58 meters long — the longest animal on Earth — what are they called?
Worm are many different distantly related bilateral animals that typically have a long cylindrical tube-like body, no limbs, and usually no eyes.
This mucolytic drug is the go-to antidote for acetaminophen overdose, working by boosting glutathione to neutralize the drug's toxic byproducts — what is it?
Acetylcysteine: Medication used to treat overdose of paracetamol.
Twice President of the Swiss Confederation, this Social Democratic politician left the Federal Council in 2023 to become Secretary General of the Council of Europe — who is he?
Alain Berset: Swiss Federal Councillor from 2012 to 2023.

Native to South Africa's Western Cape, this flowering bulb genus lends its common name to popular winter houseplants that actually belong to a different genus, Hippeastrum — which bulb, also called the naked lady or Jersey lily?
Amaryllis: Genus of plants. Amaryllis is the only genus in the subtribe Amaryllidinae (tribe Amaryllideae).
Named from Greek words for 'curved' and 'vertebra,' this type of arthritis causes long-term inflammation where the spine meets the pelvis — what is it?
Ankylosing spondylitis: Type of arthritis of the spine. Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is a type of arthritis from the disease spectrum of axial spondyloarthritis.
Native to the Philippines and spread by Austronesian voyagers as early as 1500 BCE, this palm's fruit is chewed with slaked lime and betel leaves for its stimulant effects — which species?
Areca catechu: Species of palm. It was carried widely through the tropics by the Austronesian migrations and trade since at least 1500 BCE due to its use in betel nut chewing.

Despite its name being something of a misnomer, this herding dog breed was developed in California and takes its name from imported collies that arrived alongside sheep from Down Under — what breed is it?
Australian Shepherd: American breed of dog. The Australian Shepherd, also known as the Aussie, is a breed of herding dog from the United States.
With more than 2,000 species and petals but no sepals, this flowering plant genus originated in Africa and is popular as an ornamental houseplant in cooler climates — which genus?
Begonia: Genus of perennial flowering plants.

Despite its name, this African animal's hide actually ranges from brown to grey, and it's distinguished from its 'white' cousin by a pointed, hooked upper lip rather than a wide, square one — which species?
Black rhinoceros: Species of mammal. Although the species is referred to as black, its colours vary from brown to grey.
Named for its unusually long forelimbs — Greek for 'arm lizard' — this Late Jurassic sauropod was first described in 1903 from fossils found in Colorado — which dinosaur?
Brachiosaurus: Sauropod dinosaur genus from the late Jurassic Period.
Alongside HTML and JavaScript, which style sheet language handles the layout, colors, and fonts of a webpage — separating presentation from content?
CSS: Style sheet language. CSS is a cornerstone technology of the World Wide Web, alongside HTML and JavaScript.

Time called her the "literary godmother" to Paris's Lost Generation, and her Black Sun Press printed early Hemingway and Henry Miller — but she also patented the first successful modern bra. Who was she?
Usually arising from damage to the developing brain before birth, this group of childhood movement disorders causes stiff or weak muscles, tremors, and poor coordination — what condition?
Cerebral palsy: Movement disorders that appear in early childhood.
Selected from over 11,000 applicants for NASA's Teacher in Space Project, this Concord, New Hampshire educator died aboard the Challenger in 1986 — who was she?
Christa McAuliffe: American teacher and astronaut (1948–1986)
Found naturally in the sap of the opium poppy, this opiate is a prodrug of morphine often paired with paracetamol to treat mild pain, coughs, and even diarrhea — what is it?
Codeine: Opiate and prodrug of morphine used to treat pain. It usually starts working after half an hour, with maximum effect at two hours.
This transparent structure at the front of the eye provides about two-thirds of its focusing power and can be reshaped with LASIK surgery — what is it?
Cornea: Transparent front layer of the eye. The cornea is the transparent front part of the eye which covers the iris, pupil, and anterior chamber.
Native to South and Southeast Asia and often sold as fresh stems, this tropical plant known as West Indian lemon grass can't survive a frost — what is it?
A fluorinated glucocorticoid, this medication treats everything from severe allergies and asthma to brain swelling and croup, and is given to ease preterm-labor outcomes — what is it?
Dexamethasone: Corticosteroid medication. The effects of dexamethasone are frequently seen within a day and last for about three days.
Also called Trisomy 21, this condition is caused by an extra copy of a single chromosome and grows more likely with a mother's age — from under 0.1% at 20 to about 3% at 45. What is it?
This unit of energy equals the kinetic energy a single electron gains while crossing an electric potential difference of one volt — what is it called?
Sometimes abbreviated ETM, this antibiotic treats everything from respiratory infections to syphilis and is the eye ointment routinely dabbed on newborns to prevent eye infections. What is it?
Erythromycin: Antibiotic medication. Erythromycin (sometimes abbreviated ETM in reports) is an antibiotic used for the treatment of a number of bacterial infections.
Native to the Iberian Peninsula and introduced to hundreds of locations worldwide, this grassland herbivore digs extensive burrow networks called warrens — what is it?
Belonging to the genus Abies, these evergreen conifers have cones that stand upright like candles and disintegrate at maturity, and some varieties serve as Christmas trees — which conifer genus?
Fir: Genus of coniferous trees. The genus is most closely related to Keteleeria, a small genus confined to eastern Asia.
This cold-weather injury turns skin white or waxy-blue after tissue actually freezes, often preceded by a tingling, numb warning stage called frostnip — what is it?
Frostbite: Effect of low temperature on skin and other tissues.

Predicted by Mendeleev in 1869 under the placeholder name 'ekasilicon' and discovered in 1886 by Clemens Winkler, this metalloid element was named for its discoverer's home country — what element is it?
Germanium: Chemical element with atomic number 32 (Ge)
This branch of discrete mathematics studies structures made of vertices connected by edges, modeling pairwise relationships between objects — what field is it?

Graph theory: Area of discrete mathematics. In mathematics and computer science, graph theory is the study of graphs, which are mathematical structures used to model pairwise relations between objects.

This prehensile, multi-fingered body part sits at the end of primates' forelimbs — koalas famously have two opposable thumbs on each one, while raccoons are often said to have them despite lacking true opposable thumbs. What is it?
Hand: Extremity at the end of an arm or forelimb.
Also known as the cane spider or giant crab spider, this huntsman species native to the tropics has spread to subtropical regions worldwide — what is it?
Heteropoda venatoria: Species of spider. It is native to the tropical regions of the world, and it is present in some subtropical areas as an introduced species.
Marketed as Hydrodiuril, this medication treats high blood pressure and fluid retention by blocking sodium and chloride reabsorption in the kidneys' distal tubules — what drug is it?

Hydrochlorothiazide: Diuretic medication. Hydrochlorothiazide, sold under the brand name Hydrodiuril among others, is a diuretic medication used to treat hypertension and swelling due to fluid build-up.
First described to Europeans in 1812, this reddish-brown African antelope's males sport lyre-shaped horns up to three feet long — which animal?
Impala: Species of antelope found in Africa.

This Scottish physicist's equations unified electricity, magnetism, and light into a single theory — the second great unification in physics after Newton's — while also helping found statistical mechanics — who is he?
James Clerk Maxwell: Scottish physicist and mathematician (1831–1879)
Nicknamed 'Father of the National Parks,' this Scottish-born naturalist co-founded the Sierra Club and helped preserve Yosemite Valley and Sequoia National Park — who is he?
Nicknamed the 'honey bear' though unrelated to actual bears, this nocturnal rainforest mammal is the only member of its genus and a cousin of raccoons and coatis — which arboreal creature?
This genus of bacteria mainly infects amoebae but can cause a pneumonia-like illness in humans when it spreads via poorly maintained cooling towers — what genus is it?
Legionella: Pathogenic genus of Gram-negative bacteria.
Only about 35 atoms of this synthetic element (number 116) had ever been made as of 2020 — and it's named for the California national laboratory that helped discover it. Which element?
Livermorium: Chemical element with atomic number 116 (Lv)

Originally built at a Boston hospital to manage patient records, this programming language pairs directly with an integrated key-value database and now underpins Epic's electronic health records — which language?
MUMPS: Programming language. It was originally developed at Massachusetts General Hospital for managing patient medical records and hospital laboratory information systems.
The heaviest members of the squirrel family, these ground-dwelling herbivores live in groups through the summer before disappearing underground to hibernate all winter — what are they?
Marmot: Genus of mammals (large ground squirrels)
This WWII German monoplane fighter formed the backbone of the Luftwaffe alongside the Focke-Wulf Fw 190, though Allied aircrew nicknamed it after its designer — which aircraft?

Messerschmitt Bf 109: German WWII fighter aircraft family. The Messerschmitt Bf 109 is a monoplane fighter aircraft that was designed and initially produced by the German aircraft manufacturer Bayerische Flugzeugwerke (BFW).
Awarded the 1976 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences, this University of Chicago economist championed monetarism over Keynesianism and mentored future laureates like Gary Becker — who is he?
Milton Friedman: American economist and statistician (1912–2006)
This Bangladeshi economist founded Grameen Bank and pioneered modern microcredit, winning the 2006 Nobel Peace Prize before later leading an interim government — who is he?
Muhammad Yunus: Bangladeshi economist and statesman (born 1940)
Carried harmlessly in the noses of about 10% of adults, this bacterium is the only cause of bacterial meningitis known to occur in epidemics, especially across Africa and Asia — which microbe?
Neisseria meningitidis: Species of bacterium that can cause meningitis.
Named for the daring Doolittle airmen of World War II, this subsonic stealth flying wing is being built to replace the B-1 and B-2 by 2040 — which aircraft is it?
Northrop Grumman B-21 Raider: American stealth bomber aircraft.

This dental specialty treats misaligned teeth and jaws, a condition worldwide diets of softer foods have made even more common by leaving smaller jaws with less room to fit them. What specialty is it?
Sold under the brand name Paxil, this SSRI antidepressant treats conditions from panic disorder to PTSD, and is also prescribed for premature ejaculation and menopausal hot flashes — what is it?
Paroxetine: SSRI antidepressant. It has also been used in the treatment of premature ejaculation, and hot flashes due to menopause.
Characterized by an enduring, inflexible pattern of behavior and thinking that deviates from social norms, this mental health classification impairs relationships and self-concept?
Personality disorder: Maladaptive patterns of behavior, cognition, and inner experience.

The most economically important member of the bromeliad family, this South American fruit became a 17th-century European symbol of luxury — and forms when many small flowers fuse into one — what is it?
Pineapple: Species of flowering plant in the family Bromeliaceae.
This deliquescent white salt helps make Dutch-process cocoa, soap, and glass, and can also turn up leaking from old alkaline batteries — what compound?
Potassium carbonate: Chemical compound. It is a white salt, which is soluble in water and forms a strongly alkaline solution.

Also known as talk therapy, this practice uses regular personal interaction to help people change behavior and improve well-being, with effects research suggests often outlast those of medication — what is it called?
Psychotherapy: Clinically applied psychology for desired behavior change.

Distinguished from its smaller cousin mainly by size rather than any strict taxonomy, this long-tailed rodent genus numbers 56 known species, with 'kangaroo' and 'bandicoot' variants named for their appearance — which rodent?
Recognizable by its long, black-and-white ringed tail, this highly social Madagascar primate lives in troops of up to 30 and is dominated by females — which species?
Ring-tailed lemur: Species of mammal from Madagascar.
A Stanford physicist who joined NASA in 1978, she became the first American woman in space in 1983 — and, at 32, the youngest American to fly there. Who is she?
Sally Ride: American physicist and astronaut (1951–2012)
With an eagle-like body perched on crane-like legs and a bare red-orange face, which African bird of prey spends most of its time hunting on foot across the savanna?
Secretarybird: Bird of prey. The secretarybird or secretary bird (Sagittarius serpentarius) is a large bird of prey that is endemic to Africa.
The brightest star in Earth's night sky, this binary system in Canis Major pairs a bright main-sequence star with a faint white dwarf companion — which star?
Sirius: Brightest star in Earth's night sky. Its name is derived from the Greek word Σείριος (Latin script: Seirios; lit. 'glowing' or 'scorching').

Made of a segmented series of bones cushioned by intervertebral discs, this defining feature of some 50,000 animal species surrounds and protects the nerve tissue running through it — what is it, also known as the backbone?
Spinal column: Bony structure found in vertebrates.

This small nocturnal marsupial has membranes stretching from its forelegs to hindlegs that let it soar between trees, and its scientific name translates to 'short-headed rope-dancer' — what animal is it?
Sugar glider: Species of Australian marsupial.
A staple from the Caribbean to Oceania to East Asia, this Araceae-family plant is prized for the starchy underground corm it grows much like a yam — what is it?
Taro: Species of plant. Taro (Colocasia esculenta) is a root vegetable.
After dropping out of Stuyvesant High School and serving in the Korean War, this economist went on to earn a PhD from Chicago and a National Humanities Medal in 2002?
Historically called the cucullaris, this large paired back muscle runs from the base of the skull to the lower spine and swings the shoulder blade — what is it?
Trapezius: Muscle between the lower spine and the shoulder blade. It moves the scapula and supports the arm.
Colorless, odorless, and practically non-toxic, this organic compound is the main nitrogen-bearing substance in mammal urine — fittingly, its name traces back to the Greek word for urine. What is it?
Urea: Organic compound. Urea, also called carbamide (because it is a diamide of carbonic acid), is an organic compound with chemical formula CO(NH2)2.
Sold under the brand names Trintellix and Brintellix, this antidepressant belongs to a drug class called serotonin modulators and stimulators — which medication?
Vortioxetine: Serotonin modulator antidepressant. Its effectiveness is viewed as similar to that of other antidepressants.

Ranging from microscopic to a record-breaking 58 meters long for one bootlace-shaped marine species, these limbless, usually eyeless invertebrates gave their name from the Old English 'wyrm' — what are they?
What is the chemical symbol for cobalt?
The symbol for cobalt is Co. Cobalt is a chemical element; it has symbol Co and atomic number 27.
The symbol for californium is Cf. Californium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Cf and atomic number 98.

In what year was Richard Harris born?
Richard Harris: Richard St John Francis Harris (1 October 1930 – 25 October 2002) was an Irish actor and singer.
In what year was Jet Li born?
Jet Li Lianjie (courtesy name Yangzhong; born 26 April 1963) is a martial artist, actor, and philanthropist.
In what year was Melanie Griffith born?
Melanie Griffith: Melanie Richards Griffith (born August 9, 1957) is an American actress.
In what year was Sofia Coppola born?
Sofia Coppola: Sofia Carmina Coppola ( KOH-pə-lə; born May 14, 1971) is an American filmmaker and former actress.
In what year was Sharon Tate born?
Sharon Tate: Sharon Marie Tate Polanski (January 24, 1943 – August 9, 1969) was an American actress and model.
In what year was Taika Waititi born?
Taika Waititi: Taika David Cohen (born 16 August 1975), known professionally as Taika Waititi ( TY-kə WY-tee-tee), is a New Zealand filmmaker, writer, actor, and comedian.
In what year was Nicholas Hoult born?
Nicholas Hoult: Nicholas Caradoc Hoult (born 7 December 1989) is an English actor.
In what year was Charles Bronson born?
Charles Bronson (born Charles Dennis Buchinsky; November 3, 1921 – August 30, 2003) was an American actor.
In what year was Sage Stallone born?
Sage Stallone: Sage Moonblood Stallone (May 5, 1976 – July 13, 2012) was an American actor.
In what year was Rashida Jones born?
